# Implementation Plan: read-member outbox-view ergonomics (crews D-001 + D-002)
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"crews-read-member-outbox-view"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-24. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <job_dir>/plan.md`.*
*Seeded from brainstorm: `.ralph/brainstorms/crews-read-member-outbox-view/` (recommended direction D-001, shipped @ `0bd1750c`).*

## Overview

The crews `read-member <name>` command ALREADY reads a member's OUTBOX (the reports it SENT:
done/progress/question/blocked), NOT its inbox — a premise the shipped brainstorm corrected with
unanimous multi-lens + direct-source agreement. So `read-member alice --all --pretty` already
shows a member's sent reports. The real operator pain is (1) **discoverability/naming** (an
experienced operator misfiled this believing `read-member` reads the inbox) and (2)
**progress-noise** (a live member outbox had 147 `progress` rows to 1 `done` row).

This plan is a crews-PLUGIN-only, **display-only** enhancement to the existing command — NOT a new
data path. It adds `--kind <k[,k...]>` and `--no-progress` display filters (with the cursor still
advancing over the unfiltered fresh set so filtered-out progress rows never resurface), rewrites
the description/usage/SKILL.md/AGENTS wording to say "the reports this member SENT / member output
/ `outbox.jsonl`", and adds a discoverable `read-member-reports` surface. Because both
brainstorm-named invisibility conditions for a bare alias are confirmed met (CLI top-level help
lists command names not aliases; per-engine SKILL.md is generated per command name not per alias),
this plan folds in **D-002**: a thin first-class `read-member-reports` command that DELEGATES to
read-member's shared handler/parser/formatter (never a forked second outbox reader). The bare-alias
D-001 path is documented as the minimal-surface fallback in Open Questions.

### Technical Constraints
- **Display-only invariant (load-bearing):** the per-crew cursor MUST advance over the unfiltered
  fresh set (`freshAll`), never the filtered display rows. Otherwise filtered-out progress rows
  resurface on the next default read. Mirrors `review-mail.js:348-352`.
- **Default CLI JSON-array shape is a contract:** unfiltered `read-member` CLI output must stay
  byte-identical to today's `JSON.stringify(fresh, null, 2)` bare array (scripts depend on it).
  Filter metadata is additive and present only when a filter flag is supplied.
- **Auth / roleVisibility unchanged:** `roleVisibility:['lead']`, slash `active-lead-session`, cli
  `open` with handler-side lead check. The filter is post-auth display logic only.
- **D-002 must share LOGIC but own its IDENTITY:** `read-member-reports` shares read-member's
  parse/filter/cursor/handler/format LOGIC via a factory/shared-core (no forked outbox reader, no
  cursor/auth drift) BUT overrides its own `name`/`description`/`usage`/`surfaces.cli.usage` and
  slash usage + error-prefix strings, so `read-member-reports --help` and its error text say
  `read-member-reports`, not `read-member` (`runtime.js:59-61` + `read-member.js:29-31`/`:125-129`).
- **Lead briefing golden is byte-compared:** `tests/golden/briefing-lead.md` embeds the
  lead cheat-sheet (`${usage} — ${description}` per lead-visible command). The wording rewrite AND
  the new lead-visible command BOTH change it; regenerate it or `tests/briefing-render.test.js`
  fails.
- **CHANGELOG + AGENTS lockstep:** crews releases prepend a `## <version>` CHANGELOG.md entry
  alongside the AGENTS.md section and the 6 version stamps.
- **SKILL.md regeneration is CI-gated:** `gen-skills.js --check` fails on drift; description/usage
  edits + the new command require re-running `gen-skills.js` (write mode).
- **`read-member emits no appendLog line`** is asserted by `command-compat-read-member.test.js:85`
  — the filter path must stay appendLog-free.

## Approach

### Architecture
Three additive layers, all in `hooks/commands/read-member.js` plus registry wiring and docs:
1. **Parse** — add `--kind` (value) + `--no-progress` (boolean) to both `parseSlash` (with the
   value-index guard) and `parseCli` (`parseCrewArgs` flags), validating kind tokens against
   `{progress,done,question,blocked}` and throwing `CommandInputError` on an invalid/missing value.
2. **Filter (display-only)** — in `handler`, rename the existing `fresh` to `freshAll`, keep the
   cursor-advance math on `freshAll`, compute `displayed = freshAll.filter(kindPredicate)`, and
   return `{ ...prev, fresh: displayed, freshAll, filtered, hiddenByFilter, cursorAdvancedTo }`.
3. **Disclose** — `formatSuccess`/`slashSuffix` surface a hidden-by-filter note on all three
   surfaces; CLI default-JSON switches to an additive object ONLY when a filter is active.

Plus **D-002 discoverability**: a new `hooks/commands/read-member-reports.js`. It must NOT naively
re-export read-member's `surfaces` object — `runtime.js:59-61` derives CLI `--help` from
`surface.usage || command.usage`, and read-member's reused `parseSlash`/`formatError` hard-code
`/read-member` in usage (`:29-31`) and error text (`:125-129`), so a bare re-export would make
`read-member-reports --help` and its errors say `read-member`. Instead, refactor read-member into a
small **command factory / shared core** parameterized by the command identity: extract the
parse/filter/cursor/handler/format LOGIC once, and have BOTH `read-member` and `read-member-reports`
build their `surfaces` + module exports (`name`, `description`, `usage`, `surfaces.cli.usage`, slash
usage + error-prefix strings) from that core with their own identity. This shares 100% of the
read/filter/cursor logic (no forked outbox reader, no cursor/auth drift) while presenting the
correct command identity in help, errors, and generated skills.

### Implementation Strategy (single serial cluster — same-plugin, can't parallelize)
Ordered so verification gates land first:
1. Parse + filter + disclosure + wording in `read-member.js` (US-001..US-003, US-005 wording).
2. D-002 `read-member-reports` delegating command + registry wiring (US-004).
3. Regenerate SKILL.md (`gen-skills.js`) + AGENTS.md section + version bump (US-006).
4. Tests for all of the above (US-007), then full `tests/run.js` green.

## Scope

### In Scope
- `--kind <k[,k...]>` and `--no-progress` display-only filters on `read-member`.
- parseSlash value-index guard for `--kind`; parseCli flags + validation.
- Cursor advances over the unfiltered fresh set; hidden-by-filter disclosure on all surfaces.
- Description/usage/SKILL.md/AGENTS wording rewrite to "sent reports / member output / outbox".
- `read-member-reports` discoverable surface (D-002 first-class delegating command; D-001 alias
  documented as fallback).
- Tests + SKILL.md regeneration + AGENTS section + version bump.

### Out of Scope
- Any change to what data read-member reads (it already reads the outbox).
- A `--sent`/`--output` MODE (rejected by unanimous lens consensus — entrenches the false premise).
- D-003 forensic delivery-context view (join member outbox + lead mailbox-history for
  delivery/consume timestamps) — deferred follow-up gated on the operator wanting those timestamps.
- Any other plugin/repo (happy, codex, ralph-overview). crews-only.
- Cross-lead per-lead cursor changes (the per-crew cursor model is unchanged).

## Risk Areas
- **Cursor regression (highest):** if cursor math is accidentally moved onto the filtered set,
  filtered-out progress rows resurface. Mitigation: explicit `cursor-advances-past-hidden-progress`
  regression test; keep `freshAll` as the cursor source.
- **Default JSON-array shape break:** a script reading the bare array breaks if filtered output
  changes the unfiltered shape. Mitigation: only emit the object form when a filter flag is set;
  test the unfiltered call still returns `[]`/bare array.
- **parseSlash name mis-binding:** `--kind question alice` would bind `question` as the member
  name without the value-index guard. Mitigation: extend the name finder + slash-parser tests for
  `--kind question alice` AND `alice --kind question`.
- **D-002 drift / identity leak:** a forked reader would diverge on cursor/auth; a naive surface
  re-export leaks `/read-member` into `read-member-reports` help/errors. Mitigation: factory/shared
  core for logic + own identity strings; a dispatcher test asserts both names hit the shared logic
  AND that `read-member-reports --help` says `read-member-reports`.
- **Lead briefing golden:** the wording rewrite + new lead-visible command both change the
  byte-compared `tests/golden/briefing-lead.md`. Mitigation: regenerate the golden in the same
  change; run the full suite to confirm.
- **Pinned command-list tests (D-002):** adding a lead-visible, cli-enabled command changes TWO
  pinned arrays in the same change — `command-registry-shape.test.js` `listCommands('lead', {})`
  AND `dispatcher-help.test.js` `CLI_SUBCOMMANDS` (`deepEqual`). Both iterate/assert exact lists.
  Missing either fails CI.
- **SKILL.md CI drift gate:** forgetting to regenerate fails `gen-skills.js --check`; the new
  `read-member-reports` skill dirs must exist (run the generator in write mode).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `read-member <name> --kind done` (slash + cli JSON + cli `--pretty`) shows only `done` rows from
   the fresh set; `--kind done,question,blocked` shows those three; `--no-progress` shows all
   non-progress rows; `--kind done --no-progress` ANDs (only non-progress rows that are also in the
   kind list — here `done`); comma-separated multi-kind is accepted. `--no-progress` shows
   legacy/missing-`kind` rows; `--kind <list>` excludes them. An empty outbox / no-fresh-rows case
   returns an empty result on every surface without error.
2. On a DEFAULT read (no `--peek`/`--all`/`--since`) with a filter that hides progress rows, the
   per-crew cursor advances to `max(freshAll.seq)`; a subsequent default read does NOT resurface
   the hidden progress rows (regression test).
3. `--kind question alice`, `alice --kind question`, and `--since 5 --kind done alice` all bind
   `alice` as the member name (parseSlash value-index guard); a missing `--kind` value errors with
   a `CommandInputError`; an invalid kind token errors.
4. The DEFAULT (unfiltered) `read-member` CLI call still emits the byte-identical bare JSON array on
   STDOUT (the legacy `tools/read-member.js` shim still emits its deprecation warning on STDERR —
   unchanged). A filtered CLI call adds filter fields additively (object form) and discloses
   `hiddenByFilter` / "no matching envelopes; cursor advanced to seq N" when a filter hides all
   fresh rows while the cursor advanced. Slash + `--pretty` surfaces disclose the hidden count
   inline. Filters compose correctly with `--all`/`--since`/`--peek` (display-only filter applies;
   cursor-advance rules for those modes are unchanged — `--peek`/`--all`/`--since` never advance).
5. `read-member-reports` (D-002) dispatches on BOTH the slash surface
   (`/read-member-reports`, `/crews:read-member-reports`, Copilot `/crews-read-member-reports`)
   and the CLI (`node tools/crews.js read-member-reports ...` + it appears in `tools/crews.js`
   top-level help) and shares read-member's read/filter/cursor/handler LOGIC (no forked outbox
   reader — verified by a dispatcher test asserting both names produce equivalent filtered output).
   It carries the same `--kind`/`--no-progress` filters. Its OWN identity is correct:
   `read-member-reports --help` (and its slash usage/error text) say `read-member-reports`, NOT
   `read-member` (asserted by the dispatcher test).
6. `read-member` (and `read-member-reports`) description + usage + generated SKILL.md (Claude
   colon `skills/` + Copilot kebab `.copilot-plugin/copilot-skills/`) + the crews `AGENTS.md`
   section + a prepended `CHANGELOG.md` `## 3.24.0` entry describe "the reports this member SENT /
   member output / `outbox.jsonl`", with the two example invocations. `gen-skills.js --check`
   passes (no drift).
6b. `tests/golden/briefing-lead.md` is regenerated to reflect the reworded `read-member` cheat-sheet
   line and the new `read-member-reports` line, so `tests/briefing-render.test.js` passes
   (`briefing-member.md` is unchanged — both commands are lead-only).
7. Tests cover the durable contracts: `command-compat-read-member.test.js` covers mixed-kind
   filtering in JSON + `--pretty`, the `--kind`+`--no-progress` AND behavior, the legacy/missing-kind
   contract (shown by `--no-progress`, excluded by `--kind`), `--kind` combined with
   `--all`/`--since`/`--peek`, the empty-outbox case, and the cursor-advances-past-hidden-progress
   regression. `command-args-parity.test.js` unknown-flag rejection still fires for read-member; the
   new flags are accepted; slash-parser cases (`/read-member --kind question alice`, `alice --kind
   question`, missing `--kind` value -> throws, `--since 5 --kind done alice`). The two pinned
   registry-derived arrays are updated (`command-registry-shape.test.js` `listCommands('lead', {})`
   + `dispatcher-help.test.js` `CLI_SUBCOMMANDS`). A new delegation/dispatcher test covers US-004.
   `read-member` still emits no `appendLog` line.
8. The crews version is bumped 3.23.2 -> 3.24.0 (6 stamps + `version.test.js`) and the full
   `plugins/crews/tests/run.js` suite passes (target < 60s on Windows at default concurrency). The
   FIRST full run is tee'd to a log per repo convention:
   `node tests/run.js 2>&1 | tee test-output-read-member-outbox-view.log` (grep the log for
   `FAIL`/`not ok` instead of re-running). Clear inherited `CREWS_*` env before running from a crew
   session.
9. Typecheck passes (`node --check` on every changed `.js` file — this plugin has no tsconfig).

## Preliminary Story Decomposition
- US-001: `--kind`/`--no-progress` parsing (parseSlash value-index guard + parseCli flags +
  validation).
- US-002: display-only filter in handler (cursor advances over `freshAll`; `displayed` rendered).
- US-003: hidden-by-filter disclosure across slash + cli-JSON (additive object) + cli `--pretty`.
- US-004: D-002 first-class delegating `read-member-reports` command + registry wiring + dispatcher
  test.
- US-005: wording rewrite (description/usage/AGENTS) + SKILL.md regeneration.
- US-006: version bump + AGENTS version section.
- US-007: tests (compat mixed-kind + cursor regression; args-parity; slash-parser; registry-shape
  lead array) + full-suite green.

(US-001..US-003, US-005..US-007 all touch `read-member.js`/registry/docs/tests in the same plugin;
US-004 touches the same files — therefore a SINGLE serial cluster. See Suggested Decomposition.)

## Suggested Decomposition

### Cluster: read-member-outbox-view
- Stories: US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005, US-006, US-007
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=`plugins/crews/hooks/commands/read-member.js`,
  `plugins/crews/hooks/commands/registry.js`, `plugins/crews/AGENTS.md`,
  `plugins/crews/CHANGELOG.md`, the 6 version-stamp files,
  `plugins/crews/tests/golden/briefing-lead.md`, `plugins/crews/tests/*` ;
  exclusive=`plugins/crews/hooks/commands/read-member-reports.js` (new); risk=high (every story
  rewrites the same small set of files + shared version/AGENTS/CHANGELOG/skill/golden outputs).
- `execution_mode` rationale: All stories mutate the same `read-member.js`, the shared `registry.js`,
  the same AGENTS.md/CHANGELOG/version stamps, and overlapping test files. Same-plugin parallel
  would collide on version-file and AGENTS/SKILL writes (per codexu AGENTS.md "Same-plugin
  parallel = conflict; must serialize"). Run as ONE serial cluster / one impl member.

Parallel handoff: `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <plan_job_dir>/plan.md --parallel --suggested-decomposition <plan_job_dir>/suggested-decomposition.json`

## Open Questions
1. **D-001 alias vs D-002 first-class command (the operator's stated main decision).** This plan
   RECOMMENDS and is written for **D-002** (first-class delegating command) because both
   brainstorm-named invisibility conditions are confirmed met in source: `tools/crews.js:11-16`
   lists command names not aliases, and `gen-skills.js:204-214` generates one SKILL.md per command
   name (no alias skill). **Cost asymmetry the Phase-4 review surfaced** (so the lead/operator can
   decide with eyes open): D-002 additionally requires (a) the factory/shared-core refactor so
   `read-member-reports` has correct help/error identity, (b) updating TWO pinned arrays
   (`command-registry-shape` lead list + `dispatcher-help` `CLI_SUBCOMMANDS`), (c) regenerating
   `briefing-lead.md` for the extra cheat-sheet line, and (d) a dispatcher/identity test. The
   **D-001 alias fallback** is much lighter and sidesteps the identity-string problem entirely (an
   alias openly dispatches to `read-member`, so help/errors naming `read-member` is acceptable):
   set `aliases:['read-member-reports']` on the `read-member.js` module export AND on the
   `registry.js` `COMMAND_DEFINITIONS` read-member entry (both required — module aliases for
   `runtime.js` slash `promptMatches`, registry aliases for `findCommand` CLI/slash resolution);
   drop the new module, the two pinned-array updates, and the dispatcher test; accept that the
   alias is invisible in `tools/crews.js` help + generates no per-engine skill. The lead/operator
   may downgrade US-004 to the alias at plan review. (Either way, the briefing-lead.md golden still
   changes because the `read-member` wording rewrite alters its cheat-sheet line.)
2. `--no-progress` legacy/missing-kind rows — DECIDED: `--no-progress` == `kind !== 'progress'`
   (legacy/missing-kind rows shown); `--kind <list>` excludes legacy/missing-kind rows; both
   together = AND. (Documented so impl + reviewer don't re-litigate.)
3. CLI default-JSON disclosure shape — DECIDED: unfiltered -> bare array (unchanged); filtered ->
   additive object `{ fresh: displayed, filteredKinds, hiddenByFilter, cursorAdvancedTo }`.
4. D-003 forensic delivery-context view — DEFERRED (out of scope), gated on the operator actually
   wanting delivery/consume timestamps.
